elements.quote: Asystematic review and meta-analysis were conducted by using PRISMA guideline.
elements.reason: The text explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review and meta-analysis.

elements.quote: A SRMA was conducted on SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: This sentence in the manuscript states the main objective/review question: investigating SSI following cesarean section and its predictors in Ethiopia.

elements.quote: This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs were included in this SRMA. Articles which lack our outcome of interest: SSI following cesarean section and its predictors were excluded from this SRMA.
elements.reason: The abstract/methods text specifies inclusion (studies reporting prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI, all observational designs) and exclusion (articles lacking the outcome of interest) criteria.

elements.quote: Both published and unpublished literatures conducted on the prevalence and/or the factors associated with the development of SSI following cesarean delivery in Ethiopia were searched via two authors (ES and MA). Eligible literatures in English language only were identified. An appropriate and comprehensive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI and Scopus was done since 2013.... The electronic literature search was last performed on September 23, 2023.
elements.reason: The manuscript lists the information sources searched (PubMed, MEDLINE, EMBASE, Google Scholar, HINARI, Scopus, grey literature) and gives the date the search was last performed.

elements.quote: Once the database results exported to mendeley reference manager and duplicate results removed, we used Newcastle-Ottawa Quality Assessment scale (NOS) adapted for observational studies to assess the quality of each study included in this SRMA [25] (S1 Table).
elements.reason: The text states that the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was used to assess study quality/risk of bias.

elements.quote: Then random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia. Cochrane Q-test and I 2 statistics were computed to assess heterogeneity among all the studies included in this SRMA.... Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias.... A forest plot format was used to present the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section with 95% CI. To identify determinant factors, we used the pooled AOR in forest plot format with its respective 95%CI.
elements.reason: The manuscript specifies the synthesis methods (random effects meta-analysis, heterogeneity assessment, publication bias tests) and presentation formats (forest plots).

elements.quote: Eventually, 19 articles were found eligible for inclusion in the final SRMA... A total of 8755 participants with the smallest 166 to the largest 1069 participants included and found the prevalence which ranges from 6.80 to 25.4% of SSI following cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The text reports the total number of included studies (19), total participants (8755) and summarizes study characteristics (designs, regional distribution, prevalence range).

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.2912.97%). Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)), chorioamnionitis (AOR = 4.26, 95% CI; (1.99-8.91)), prolonged PROM (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.51-5.62)), repeated vaginal examination (AOR = 3.80, 95% CI; (2.45-5.88)), decreased hemoglobin level (AOR = 4.57, 95%CI; (3.16-6.60)), vertical skin incision (AOR = 3.09, 95% CI; (2.04-4.67)) and general anesthesia (AOR = 1.82, 95% CI (1.21-2.75)) are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The manuscript presents main outcome results (pooled prevalence with CI) and results for associated factors, including effect estimates and CIs.

elements.quote: The pooled estimate of SSI in Ethiopia was 11.13% (95%CI, 9.2912.97%).
elements.reason: A meta-analysis was conducted and the manuscript reports the summary estimate and its 95% confidence interval.

elements.quote: Prolonged labor (AOR = 3.16, 95% CI; (2.14-4.68)) ... general anesthesia (AOR = 1.82, 95% CI (1.21-2.75)) are significantly associated with SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: When comparing groups (e.g. prolonged labor vs not), the abstract/text provides direction of effect via adjusted odds ratios >1 indicating increased risk.

elements.quote: However, the substantial heterogeneity between included studies might affect the overall pooled prevalence of SSI after cesarean section (Fig 3). Thus subgroup analysis was done.
elements.reason: The manuscript notes an important limitation of the evidence (substantial heterogeneity) which may affect the pooled estimate.
No explicit general interpretation of the results or discussion of important implications is present in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: Funding: The author(s) received no specific funding for this work.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states the primary source of funding (no specific funding was received).

elements.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis were registered in the PROSPERO database with ID no. CRD42023442583.
elements.reason: The manuscript provides the registry name (PROSPERO) and the registration number.

elements.quote: Worldwide, surgery related deaths within 30 days of the procedure accounts the third contributor among all causes of deaths, with an estimated 4.2 million people annually and half of these deaths occur in low and middle income countries.
elements.reason: Provides broad global context about surgical burden but does not describe the current state of knowledge specifically about surgical site infection after cesarean section or identify important uncertainties in the literature.

elements.quote: Worldwide, surgery related deaths within 30 days of the procedure accounts the third contributor among all causes of deaths, with an estimated 4.2 million people annually and half of these deaths occur in low and middle income countries.

elements.quote: Inclusion. This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA. Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023. Exclusion. which lack our outcome of interest: SSI following cesarean section and its predictors were excluded from this SRMA. On the other hand, literatures with poor quality as per the criteria of reviewing articles were excluded from this SRMA.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes overall inclusion and exclusion criteria (study designs, population, time frame, outcome, language) and exclusion for poor quality, which indicates how studies were selected for the review/meta-analysis in general.
